title: rollback-hypothesis-evaluator-and-causal-state-mender
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce an automated rollback hypothesis evaluator and causal state mender that fuses cost/latency/quality signals into robust rollback triggers, and performs safe state reconciliation for components (KV cache prefixes, routing policies, and batching config) after automated reverts. Goal is to reduce manual intervention for costly regressions while avoiding noisy or premature rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: A hypothesis evaluator that consumes at least 6 telemetry signals (token-cost delta, per-route latency p95, error-rate, live-eval quality drop, autoscaler saturation, model-variance) and produces a rollback probability score
Config apply events flagged with score >= 0.85 trigger a controlled rollback flow with staged prefix quarantine and a 3-minute cooldown window

State mender reconciles KV cache entries affected by the change: quarantined prefixes are invalidated and a background safe-recover process restores known-good prefetched prefixes without causing traffic storms
Rollback actions are annotated in change logs and visible in Console; token-level cost impact and incident timeline are recorded for each triggered rollback
Simulator harness (see links) reproduces 3 historical incidents and matches human-verified rollback decisions in at least 2/3 cases
implementation_notes: Signal ingestion: extend existing telemetry aggregator to add derived signals (cost-per-token rolling-window, batch occupancy distribution)
Hypothesis evaluator: lightweight rules + logistic regression ensemble (initially) deployed as a sidecar service with a 100ms decision budget
Guardrails: require minimum sample size and stable baseline window; disable automated rollback for changes flagged by 'no-auto-revert' tag
Safe apply flow: staged shadow apply -> rate-limited rollout -> monitor window -> conditional commit or rollback
State reconciliation: implement prefix quarantine store that tracks invalidated prefixes and exposes a safe-recover API to rehydrate prefix cache from snapshot or warm prefetched candidates
Auditability: every decision must include signal snapshot, model weights used by evaluator, and PR/commit refs

risks: False positives: aggressive sensitivity could cause unnecessary rollbacks and customer-visible regressions
Signal drift: models trained on historical incidents may not generalize to new failure modes
Recovery storms: naive cache rehydration could produce thundering herd on downstream model endpoints
Operational complexity: more moving parts increases incident surface area and SRE cognitive load
qa_plan: Unit tests for signal normalization and scoring function
Replay tests using production telemetry snapshots from 3 prior incidents (stored in S3), verify evaluator score matches expected thresholds
Chaos test: introduce synthetic cost spike during staged shadow apply and assert rollback triggers within 120s
Load test: safe-recover API must rehydrate 10k prefixes without exceeding downstream QPS budget (simulate with load generator)
